letter:
Dear Gastroenterologist,

Re: Felicity Archer, 38

Felicity was diagnosed with coeliac disease on duodenal biopsy in 2022. She has followed a strict gluten-free diet with a dietitian's help and her symptoms have resolved. Her tTG has normalised and her iron studies, B12, folate and vitamin D are all normal. Bone density last year was normal. She has moved to the area and would like ongoing specialist follow-up as recommended by her previous gastroenterologist.

Kind regards,
Dr Nathaniel Okoro
note: Well-controlled coeliac disease being transferred for follow-up is routine.

letter:
Dear Dermatologist,

Re: Omar Haddad, 27

Omar has had vitiligo for about four years, with symmetrical patches on his hands, elbows and around his eyes. The patches have been stable in size for over a year. He has tried a potent topical steroid and topical tacrolimus with only slight repigmentation. Thyroid function is normal. He finds the patches on his hands affect his confidence at work and would like to discuss phototherapy or other options.

Regards,
Dr Katrina Velasquez
note: Stable vitiligo with a treatment question is routine; it is cosmetic and not deteriorating.

letter:
Dear Orthopaedic Surgeon,

Re: Gwen Ridley, 71

Gwen has right knee osteoarthritis with severe medial joint space loss and osteophytes on X-ray. Over the last year her pain has become constant and wakes her most nights. She can walk only about 100 metres and now needs a stick and a rail for steps. She has completed a supervised exercise programme, lost 5 kg, and had two steroid injections with brief benefit. She is otherwise fit and would like to discuss knee replacement.

Kind regards,
Dr Desmond Achterberg
note: Severe, disabling knee osteoarthritis after failed conservative care is semi-urgent: chronic and degenerative but with significant dysfunction.

letter:
Dear Respiratory Physician,

Re: Darren Pitcher, 61

Darren has had asthma since childhood and finds his preventer less effective lately; he is on budesonide-formoterol and would like to review his inhaler technique and options. He is a current smoker, about 35 pack-years, and is trying to quit with varenicline. He mentioned in passing that he has coughed up bright red blood on several mornings over the past three weeks. Chest X-ray is booked for next week. He has otherwise been well.

Regards,
Dr Ophelia Strand
note: Haemoptysis in a heavy smoker raises suspicion of lung cancer, so this is urgent despite the asthma-review framing.

letter:
Dear Neurologist,

Re: Mei Lin Zhou, 44

Mei Lin has had tension-type headaches for years, typically at the end of a working day, which respond to paracetamol. She asked for a referral to discuss whether she needs a preventer as she is using analgesia about eight days a month. On review today she also told me her left hand has become steadily weaker over the past three weeks; she has dropped two cups and struggles with her keyboard. I found reduced grip and finger extension on the left. She is otherwise well.

Kind regards,
Dr Wallace Abernathy
note: Progressive weakness with a new neurological deficit is urgent, even though the letter is about long-standing tension headaches.

letter:
Dear Orthopaedic Surgeon,

Re: Aaron Whitlock, 46

Aaron felt a pop in the front of his right elbow while lifting a washing machine four days ago. He has bruising in the forearm, a bulge in the upper arm and weak, painful supination. The hook test is negative. MRI yesterday shows a complete distal biceps tendon rupture with 3 cm retraction. He is a right-handed carpenter and is keen to return to work.

Regards,
Dr Josephine Maddox
note: A complete distal biceps rupture four days old needs a time-critical decision on repair, so it is urgent.

letter:
Dear Orthopaedic Surgeon,

Re: Nicholas Fenwick, 33

Nicholas has had pain at the lower pole of his left kneecap for about two years, which he gets only when jumping in social volleyball. He works full time, walks and cycles without trouble and sleeps well. Ultrasound shows chronic patellar tendinopathy without a tear. Eighteen months of eccentric loading with a physiotherapist has helped partly. He has read about surgical debridement and would like to know if he is a candidate.

Kind regards,
Dr Henrietta Oyelaran
note: Chronic patellar tendinopathy with minimal dysfunction is routine; considering surgery does not make it time-critical.

letter:
Dear Respiratory Physician,

Re: Lionel Jacobsen, 73

Lionel asked me to follow up his referral from June about his COPD, as he has not heard anything. His condition is unchanged: FEV1 58% predicted, breathless on hills, one exacerbation treated with prednisolone this year. He is an ex-smoker on tiotropium-olodaterol. He would like to discuss pulmonary rehabilitation and whether his inhalers can be improved.

Kind regards,
Dr Marguerite Collins

history.note: June 2026: Referred to respiratory for COPD review, triaged routine.

note: A chaser for the same unchanged COPD already on the routine list; no new entry and no change.

letter:
Dear Neurologist,

Re: Bethany Kowal, 22

I saw Bethany today after her attendance at ED on Sunday with a first generalised seizure. I understand the ED team have already referred her to your clinic. I am writing to confirm the details: the seizure was witnessed by her flatmate and lasted about a minute, CT brain was normal and bloods were unremarkable. She has had no further events and is not driving. There is no family history of epilepsy.

Regards,
Dr Samuel Ferrante

history.note: Monday: ED referral to neurology for first generalised seizure, triaged urgent.
August 2026: Referred to cardiology for palpitations, Holter showed ectopics only, triaged routine.

note: The first seizure is already listed as urgent and the patient's separate cardiology entry is unrelated; both stay unchanged with no new entry.

letter:
Dear Dermatologist,

Re: Garry Whitfield, 69

Garry is on your list for a lesion on his right forearm that I thought was a seborrhoeic keratosis. It has changed considerably over the past six weeks. It has roughly doubled in size to 15 mm, become raised and dome-shaped with a central crust, and it bled twice this week. It is tender to touch. He had a squamous cell carcinoma removed from his scalp in 2022.

Kind regards,
Dr Penelope Adair

history.note: May 2026: Referred to dermatology for a lesion on the right forearm, ?seborrhoeic keratosis, triaged routine.
2022: Excision of scalp squamous cell carcinoma.

note: A rapidly growing, bleeding lesion is urgent; the existing routine dermatology entry should be updated to urgent, not duplicated.

letter:
Dear Cardiologist,

Re: Maureen Gallagher, 76

You have Maureen on your list for moderate aortic stenosis with mild breathlessness. Her symptoms have worsened. Last week she fainted while walking up the slope from the car park, and she now gets chest tightness after one block. Her repeat echo shows severe aortic stenosis, peak velocity 4.6 m/s, mean gradient 48 mmHg, with preserved LV function. She lives alone and is otherwise independent.

Regards,
Dr Laurence Hepburn

waitlist.problem: moderate aortic stenosis with exertional breathlessness

history.note: March 2026: Referred to cardiology for moderate aortic stenosis with exertional breathlessness, triaged semi-urgent.

note: Severe symptomatic aortic stenosis with exertional syncope is urgent; the existing semi-urgent entry should be raised, not duplicated.

letter:
Dear Neurologist,

Re: Harvey Lindgren, 54

I referred Harvey a month ago with progressive weakness and numbness in both legs. He has been seeing a physiotherapist and feels his walking is a little better and he is less worried. As he is improving, I wonder whether his appointment could be moved to routine to free up an urgent slot for someone else. I have not re-examined him in detail since the referral.

Kind regards,
Dr Celeste Mwangi

waitlist.problem: progressive bilateral leg weakness and numbness

history.note: October 2026: Referred to neurology for progressive bilateral leg weakness and numbness, triaged urgent.

note: The guideline forbids lowering urgency on a letter alone; the urgent entry stays and the request is flagged.

letter:
Dear Gastroenterologist,

Re: Rodney Featherstone, 60

Rodney had a colonoscopy at a private hospital last month and I would be grateful if you could see him to discuss the findings and the histology, which I have attached. He is otherwise in good health and takes rosuvastatin. Please advise on follow-up.

Kind regards,
Dr Adele Brennan
note: The colonoscopy findings and histology are not included and no symptoms are given, so the GP must be asked before a category can be set.

letter:
Dear Doctor,

Re: Candice Morley, 49

Thank you for seeing Candice with the problem we discussed on the phone yesterday. I would appreciate your review at your earliest convenience. She has a background of hypothyroidism on thyroxine and is a non-smoker. She works as a bookkeeper and is happy to attend any clinic.

Regards,
Dr Gordon Abeysekera
note: The letter describes neither the problem nor the clinic needed, so the GP must be asked before booking.

letter:
Dear Psychiatrist,

Re: Elliot Raine, 35

Elliot has had recurrent major depression since his twenties. He has tried sertraline, escitalopram and venlafaxine at adequate doses, with only partial response, and has seen a psychologist for CBT for a year. He is working but struggling, with low mood, poor sleep and loss of interest. He denies suicidal intent and has good support at home. I would value your advice on treatment-resistant depression.

Kind regards,
Dr Miranda Esposito

waitlist.problem: new atrial fibrillation with heart failure symptoms

note: Psychiatry is not run by this service, so nothing is booked and the referral is flagged for redirection.

letter:
Dear Respiratory Physician,

Re: Archie Sullivan, 8

Archie has had asthma since he was four. Despite a fluticasone preventer and a spacer, used correctly, he has needed two courses of oral prednisolone this winter and wakes with cough three nights a week. He misses sport at school. His parents are keen for specialist review of his asthma control and whether he needs a step up in treatment.

Regards,
Dr Yolanda Fischer
note: An 8-year-old needs paediatrics, which this adult service does not run; it must not be booked into respiratory and is flagged for redirection.

letter:
Dear Doctor,

Re: Dorothy Ingram, 74

I would be grateful for two reviews. Dorothy has been tired and breathless on exertion for two months. Bloods show Hb 96, MCV 71 and ferritin 5, consistent with iron deficiency anaemia. She has no obvious bleeding, is not on anticoagulants, and has never had a colonoscopy or gastroscopy. Separately, she has mild facial rosacea with redness and occasional papules, stable for years on metronidazole gel, and would like advice about laser treatment.

Kind regards,
Dr Benedict Saunders
note: Iron deficiency anaemia in an older patient is urgent gastroenterology; stable mild rosacea is routine dermatology; both are booked.

letter:
Dear Doctor,

Re: Warwick Templeton, 58

Warwick has mild asthma diagnosed in adulthood, well controlled on as-needed budesonide-formoterol, using it about twice a month. His spirometry is normal and he has had no exacerbations. He would like a specialist to confirm the diagnosis because he is applying for a commercial diving licence. He also has bothersome urinary frequency, a weak stream and nocturia three times a night; PSA is normal. I would appreciate a urology opinion regarding his prostate.

Regards,
Dr Fiona Chatterjee
note: Well-controlled mild asthma is routine respiratory; the prostate symptoms need urology, which is not run here, so that part is flagged.

letter:
Dear Gastroenterologist,

Re: Sienna Calloway, 28

Please see as an URGENT case. Sienna has had crampy lower abdominal pain and bloating with alternating constipation and loose stools for two years, worse with stress and relieved by opening her bowels. There is no bleeding, weight loss or night-time symptoms. FBC, CRP, coeliac serology and faecal calprotectin are all normal. She is frustrated and has asked for an urgent specialist appointment.

Kind regards,
Dr Russell Hammond

waitlist.problem: unexplained weight loss with bowel change

note: Typical irritable bowel symptoms with normal tests and no red flags are routine, whatever the GP asks for.

letter:
Dear Gastroenterologist,

Re: Leonard Ashby, 77

No hurry with Leonard, a routine appointment will be fine as he is quite stoic. He has had increasing fatigue over three months and has lost about 5 kg without trying. Bloods show Hb 98, MCV 72, ferritin 6. He takes aspirin 100 mg for previous stents but no other blood thinners. He reports no obvious bleeding. His last colonoscopy was ten years ago and was normal.

Regards,
Dr Charlotte Weston
note: Iron deficiency anaemia with weight loss in an older patient is urgent, even though the GP says routine is fine.
